name: AUTOMATIC FILM COATING MACHINE
desc: Tabletop Automatic Film Coating Machine engineered for high-precision thin film research and battery electrode coating. Features an integrated heavy-duty vacuum aluminum plate paired with an in-built oil-free vacuum pump and a 200 mm width doctor blade assembly.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS AUTOMATIC FILM COATING MACHINE is a high-precision benchtop thin-film deposition and drying system engineered for controlled doctor-blade casting of ceramic, polymer, perovskite, and battery electrode slurries. Its heavy-duty vacuum aluminum plate with integrated oil-free pump immobilizes flexible substrates such as copper foil, aluminum foil, ITO glass, or PEN film, preventing wrinkles during linear coating. A 200 mm doctor blade with micrometer gap adjustment from 0.01 to 3.5 mm defines wet film thickness; the brushless drive translates the blade or substrate at 0–100 mm/s with ±10 mm/s accuracy to control shear rate and final dry film uniformity. An integrated PID-controlled heated bed from ambient to 200 °C (±1 °C) drives solvent evaporation and annealing. The color touch-screen controller manages stroke length (10–250 mm), speed profiles, and digital timing. This platform is used by B.Sc/M.Sc students, PhD researchers, doctoral scientists, and chemists in lithium-ion battery R&D to coat NMP-based slurries containing LiFePO4, LiCoO2, LiNiMnCoO2 (NMC), graphite, carbon black, PVDF binder, and conductive additives; in perovskite and organic photovoltaic work with DMF/DMSO/PbI2 formulations; in ceramic processing with alumina, YSZ, TiO2, and sol-gel slurries; and in corrosion and metallurgical studies with acidic or alkaline sols. It supports process development aligned with ISO 1517 / ASTM D823 draw-down and coating thickness practice, enabling reproducible electrode films, membrane casts, and thin-film sensor fabrication.
sop: Wear nitrile gloves, safety goggles, and a lab coat; verify fume hood extraction is active if using solvent-based slurries such as NMP, DMF, or acetone.
Clean the vacuum plate and doctor blade with lint-free tissue and isopropyl alcohol; place the substrate (copper foil, aluminum foil, ITO glass, etc.) flat and centered on the vacuum plate.
Switch ON the main power isolator, then activate the oil-free vacuum pump using the touch-screen 'VACUUM' button; confirm the substrate is held without wrinkles.
Set the required stroke length (10–250 mm) using the adjustable position switches on the guide rail.
Set the coating speed on the color touch-screen display, e.g. 10–50 mm/s for battery slurries.
Loosen the doctor blade micrometer, set the wet film thickness from 0.01 to 3.5 mm using the digital thickness gauge, then lock the blade.
Press the 'SET' button once on the digital PID temperature controller.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter, for example 80 °C for NMP-based electrode drying or 150 °C for annealing.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value; wait until the actual temperature stabilizes within ±1 °C before coating.
Set the in-built electronic digital timer to the required drying or annealing dwell time.
Pour or syringe a small amount of slurry just in front of the doctor blade, avoiding large excesses that can overflow the vacuum plate.
Press 'START' on the touch-screen controller to run the coating stroke; do not open the guard or touch the moving blade during operation.
After the stroke stops, allow the coated film to dry at the set temperature for the programmed time, monitoring for solvent vapor accumulation.
Switch OFF the heater, allow the plate to cool below 40 °C, then switch OFF the vacuum pump and release the substrate.
Remove the coated film carefully with a non-metallic scraper if needed; label and store it in a dry, dust-free environment.
Clean the doctor blade and vacuum plate immediately with compatible solvent or deionized water; never leave dried ceramic, polymer, or battery slurry on the blade.

Safety Warning: The heated bed, doctor blade, and vacuum plate can remain above 40 °C; solvent vapors such as NMP, DMF, or acetone are flammable and toxic—always operate with active fume extraction, keep ignition sources away, and never touch hot surfaces without thermal gloves.
